The stock market is a complex and ever-changing system, and there is no one-size-fits-all approach to investing. However, by using technical analysis, investors can gain insights into the potential direction of a stock's price and make more informed investment decisions.

The five technical analysis methods used in this report are Moving Averages, MACD (Moving Average Convergence Divergence), Fibonacci Retracement, Bollinger Bands & Relative Strength Index (RSI).

Moving Averages (MA) is a widely recognized momentum indicator that tracks the average price of a security over a specific period of time. Typically, traders make use of short-term and long-term moving averages to identify trend direction and potential trading opportunities. The moving average for this stock indicates a score of 6 out of 10, suggesting a neutral overall trend.

Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) is a trend-following momentum indicator that shows the relationship between the 12-day and 26-day exponential moving averages (EMAs) of a security's price. The MACD line is the difference between the two EMAs, and the signal line is a 9-day EMA of the MACD line. The MACD histogram is the difference between the MACD line and the signal line. The MACD for this stock indicates a score of 8 out of 10, suggesting a bullish trend.

Fibonacci Retracement is a technical analysis technique that identifies potential areas of support and resistance based on the Fibonacci sequence. The Fibonacci sequence is a series of numbers in which each number is the sum of the two preceding ones, starting from 0 and 1. The most common Fibonacci retracement levels are 23.6%, 38.2%, 50%, 61.8%, and 78.6%. The Fibonacci Retracement for this stock shows a score of 7 out of 10, indicating a potential pullback or reversal.

Bollinger Bands are a volatility indicator that measures the distance between a security's price and its moving average. The Bollinger Bands are plotted two standard deviations above and below the moving average. Bollinger Bands can be used to identify overbought and oversold conditions, as well as potential trend reversals. The Bollinger Bands indicator for this stock has a score of 8 out of 10, indicating high volatility and potential for a breakout or pullback.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is a momentum indicator that measures the magnitude of recent price changes to evaluate whether a security is overbought or oversold. The RSI is calculated by comparing the average gain of up periods to the average loss of down periods over a specified period of time. The most common RSI period is 14. The RSI for this stock indicates a score of 7 out of 10, suggesting that the stock is neither overbought nor oversold.

Overall, the technical analysis of this stock indicates a neutral trend with potential for a pullback or reversal. Investors should use this information in conjunction with other research and analysis to make informed investment decisions.
